node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Benchmark angle turns
node.description: Use quarter turns, half turns and full turns as benchmarks for comparing and estimating angle size.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Angle size independent of arm length
node.description: Recognise that an angle's size depends on the amount of turn, not on the length of its drawn arms.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Protractor vertex alignment
node.description: Place the protractor centre on the angle vertex and align the baseline with one arm before measuring.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Protractor scale selection
node.description: Choose the correct inner or outer protractor scale based on the starting arm of the angle.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Protractor measurement reasonableness check
node.description: Check whether a protractor reading is reasonable by comparing it with acute, right, obtuse, straight or reflex benchmarks.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Construct angle from starting ray
node.description: Construct an angle of a given measure by drawing a starting ray, marking the target degree measure and drawing the second ray.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Exterior angle of a triangle
node.description: Use the exterior angle relationship that an exterior angle of a triangle equals the sum of the two remote interior angles.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Isosceles triangle base angles
node.description: Use the equality of base angles in isosceles triangles to solve unknown-angle problems.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Corresponding angles in parallel lines
node.description: Recognise and use equal corresponding angles formed by a transversal cutting parallel lines.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Alternate angles in parallel lines
node.description: Recognise and use equal alternate angles formed by a transversal cutting parallel lines.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Co-interior angles in parallel lines
node.description: Recognise and use co-interior angles on parallel lines as supplementary angles.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Converse parallel angle tests
node.description: Use angle relationships such as equal corresponding or alternate angles to infer that lines are parallel.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Angle chasing equation setup
node.description: Set up and solve equations from angle relationships in multi-step diagrams.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: SOHCAHTOA memory structure
node.description: Use SOHCAHTOA as a compact way to recall the sine, cosine and tangent side-ratio definitions.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Draw right triangle model from context
node.description: Represent a contextual trigonometry problem with a labelled right-triangle diagram before choosing a ratio.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Angle of elevation
node.description: Interpret angle of elevation as the angle measured upward from a horizontal line of sight.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Angle of depression
node.description: Interpret angle of depression as the angle measured downward from a horizontal line of sight.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Bearings in right triangle contexts
node.description: Use bearings or compass directions to form right-triangle trigonometry models in navigation contexts.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Multi-step right triangle trigonometry problems
node.description: Solve problems requiring more than one trigonometric, Pythagorean or angle relationship in right-triangle contexts.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Trigonometry solution reasonableness
node.description: Check whether trigonometric side lengths or angles are reasonable using triangle geometry, units and context.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Rounding trigonometry answers
node.description: Round trigonometry answers appropriately while preserving units and enough working precision.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Angle size is amount of turn
node.description: An angle measures the amount of turn between two rays, not the length of the rays drawn.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Straight line angles sum to 180 degrees
node.description: Adjacent angles on a straight line have measures that add to 180 degrees.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Co-interior angles sum to 180 degrees
node.description: Co-interior angles formed by a transversal across parallel lines are supplementary.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Elevation and depression use horizontal reference
node.description: Angles of elevation and depression are measured from a horizontal line of sight.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Longer arms mean larger angle
node.description: Learner judges angle size by the length of the drawn arms rather than the amount of turn.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Wrong protractor scale selected
node.description: Learner reads the wrong protractor scale, producing a complementary or supplementary-looking measurement error.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Co-interior angles treated as equal
node.description: Learner treats co-interior angles on parallel lines as equal rather than supplementary.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Elevation or depression measured from vertical
node.description: Learner measures angle of elevation or depression from a vertical line rather than the horizontal line of sight.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Ratio selected from target side only
node.description: Learner chooses a trigonometric ratio based only on the unknown side rather than the pair of known and unknown sides relative to the angle.

edge.rationale: Accurate vertex alignment is central to measuring angles with a protractor.
Alternate angles are a core parallel-line transversal relationship.
Applied right-triangle trigonometry directly practises modelling contexts as right triangles.
Angle-of-elevation contexts are common right-triangle trigonometry applications.
Benchmark turns depend on understanding angles as turns.
edge.failure_signal: Learner compares drawn arm lengths rather than turn amounts.

edge.rationale: Recognising angle size as independent of arm length depends on the turn model of angle.
edge.failure_signal: Learner says a longer drawn arm makes the angle larger.

edge.rationale: Using a protractor depends on reading degree units and aligning the measurement tool.
edge.failure_signal: Learner does not align the protractor centre and baseline before reading degrees.

edge.rationale: Correct scale choice comes after the protractor is aligned to the starting arm.
edge.failure_signal: Learner reads the scale that starts from the opposite side of the protractor.

edge.rationale: Reasonableness checks use angle classifications such as acute, right and obtuse.
edge.failure_signal: Learner accepts a 140 degree reading for an obviously acute angle.

edge.rationale: Constructing an angle uses the same alignment and scale-selection skills as measuring with a protractor.
edge.failure_signal: Learner marks the correct measure but draws the ray from the wrong vertex or baseline.

edge.rationale: The exterior angle relationship follows from triangle angle sum and straight-line angles.
edge.failure_signal: Learner treats the exterior angle as equal to the adjacent interior angle.

edge.rationale: Isosceles base-angle reasoning is usually combined with triangle angle sum to solve diagrams.
edge.failure_signal: Learner assumes any two triangle angles are equal without side information.

edge.rationale: Corresponding angles are one of the named angle-pair types in parallel-line transversal diagrams.
edge.failure_signal: Learner cannot match angle positions across the two intersections.

edge.rationale: Alternate-angle reasoning extends recognition of angle-pair positions in parallel-line diagrams.
edge.failure_signal: Learner confuses alternate angles with adjacent or corresponding angles.

edge.rationale: Co-interior angle reasoning is another parallel-line relationship after equal angle pairs.
edge.failure_signal: Learner treats co-interior angles as equal rather than summing to 180 degrees.

edge.rationale: Converse parallel tests require recognising angle-pair relationships first.
edge.failure_signal: Learner assumes lines are parallel without a valid angle relationship.

edge.rationale: Equation setup in angle chasing depends on knowing the underlying angle relationships.
edge.failure_signal: Learner writes equations that do not match the diagram relationships.

edge.rationale: SOHCAHTOA requires identifying hypotenuse, opposite and adjacent sides.
edge.failure_signal: Learner recalls letters but cannot connect them to side names.

edge.rationale: Drawing a contextual right-triangle model requires labelling the right triangle and its relevant sides.
edge.failure_signal: Learner starts calculating without a diagram and mismatches sides or angles.

edge.rationale: Elevation contexts require modelling a line of sight and horizontal reference in a right triangle.
edge.failure_signal: Learner measures the angle from vertical or labels the wrong side as horizontal distance.

edge.rationale: Depression contexts use the same horizontal line-of-sight convention as elevation, measured downward.
edge.failure_signal: Learner does not recognise the alternate interior relationship between elevation and depression angles.

edge.rationale: Bearing contexts must be represented diagrammatically before applying right-triangle trigonometry.
edge.failure_signal: Learner uses the bearing angle directly without locating the right triangle and reference direction.

edge.rationale: Multi-step trig problems build on single-step missing-side calculations.
edge.failure_signal: Learner can do one ratio calculation but cannot plan multiple steps from the diagram.

edge.rationale: Reasonableness checks require interpreting calculated angles and side lengths in triangle context.
edge.failure_signal: Learner accepts impossible values such as an acute right-triangle angle over 90 degrees.

edge.rationale: Rounding should preserve a reasonable contextual answer with appropriate units.
edge.failure_signal: Learner rounds too early or omits units and context.
